report.question: 任意指定的同号局部扰动为何能迫使周期轨道或极小超曲面进入扰动区域，谱增长又在哪些维数和假设下足以证明这一点？
report.reading_scope: Read the entire published report, sections 1–8 and references. Checked quantifiers, dimensions, rationality, perturbation composition, genus-limit order, announcement status, and conditional orbifold assumptions. Section 8 is integrated in 2H0P–2H0S and linked to the Chodosh branch.

proof_scope.2H04: Positive lower period bound and closedness of the finite-sum action spectrum proved; its nullity is cited from Irie Lemma 4.1, not inferred from arbitrary sums of null sets.
proof_scope.2H05: C0 continuity deduced from monotonicity and conformality; existence of ECH spectral selectors is cited.
proof_scope.2H07: Strong closing derived from ECH class existence, spectral axioms, null spectrum and the Weyl law; these deep inputs are cited, not reconstructed.
proof_scope.2H08: Negative perturbations proved by applying the three-dimensional theorem at the endpoint form and reversing the parameter.
proof_scope.2H09: Cotangent Hamilton equations, geodesic projection and the conformal factor one-half derived; the three-dimensional strong closing theorem is applied.
proof_scope.2H0C: Rationality of Hamiltonian surface maps proved by an explicit mapping-torus trivialization; the PFH closing theorem is cited.
proof_scope.2H0D: Reeb rotation formula, common-period criterion and the n-simple-orbit statement for pairwise irrational axis ratios proved directly.
proof_scope.2H0F: Simultaneous rational approximation and radial pullback explicitly prove the Hofer near-periodic estimate.
proof_scope.2H0I: The endpoint theorem is cited; conjugacy of left/right composition and the implication to strong closing are proved.
proof_scope.2H0J: Generic equidistribution is cited; density and normalized time-measure consequences are proved.
proof_scope.2H0L: Small-ball capacity inequality and telescoping small-gap implication proved using cited elementary-capacity properties and ball normalization.
proof_scope.2H0O: Local Darboux proof includes a radial primitive, the Moser vector field, local flow control, and coordinate verification of Cartan and pullback differentiation.
proof_scope.2H0P: Definitions of flat boundaries, k-sweepouts and widths recalled; Almgren topology, finiteness, min-max existence and smooth realization are cited inputs.
proof_scope.2H0Q: Bilinear-metric scaling, comparison bounds, C0 continuity and strict conformal volume growth proved; the volume-spectrum Weyl law is cited.
proof_scope.2H0R: The local perturbation conclusion is deduced from cited smooth min-max realization, bumpy-metric countability (now linked to 2H0S) and the Weyl law. The ambient range 3–7 and bumpy base metric remain explicit.
proof_scope.2H0S: Jacobi-kernel nondegeneracy and bumpy metrics defined separately. White genericity and Sharp bounded-area/index finiteness cited via Irie–Marques–Neves Proposition 3.1; countability follows by taking a countable union. Neither analytic theorem is claimed proved locally.

deferred: ECH and PFH analytic constructions, their cobordism maps, Weyl asymptotics and existence of suitable homology classes remain precise cited inputs.
The CP2 pseudoholomorphic interpolation argument in section 5.4, including Gromov compactness and transversality, is cited through the slow-growth result rather than expanded as a full proof.
General contact-manifold elementary spectral invariants beyond Liouville boundaries are referenced, not independently reconstructed.
The section 7.1 alpha-strong closing problem and the Katok-type near-periodic examples are not expanded into separate branches.
Orbifold Gromov-Witten and SFT Assumption 1.3 is retained; no unconditional general Hofer near-periodic theorem is claimed.
High-dimensional modified-capacity results remain announcements because the report cites an in-preparation manuscript.

Almgren-Pitts compactness, interpolation, regularity, White bumpy-metric theory and Sharp compactness are cited. General min-max construction and higher-dimensional singular variants are not claimed proved locally.
Generic minimal-hypersurface equidistribution, Song's general infinitude theorem and the detailed two-dimensional width computation are not expanded.
